author: SInow
title: Miguel Rojas Retires from MLB After Dodgers' NLCS Loss | Sports
text:
Los Angeles Dodgers infielder Miguel Rojas officially announces his retirement from Major League Baseball following the team's Game 4 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks in the National League Championship Series. The 37-year-old, a two-time World Series champion, played his final game at Chase Field and expressed interest in remaining with the Dodgers organization as a coach or future manager.
Sep 24, 2025; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers first base Enrique Hernández , shortstop Mookie Betts , first base Freddie Freeman , and Miguel Rojas in the seventh inning against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field.
Mandatory Credit: Rick Scuteri-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters ConnectThe loss has also officially ended the career of Miguel Rojas. After the Dodgers' 6-4 loss in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series, Rojas told reporters that he's retiring from Major League Baseball.throughout the year, saying he would consider continuing his playing career if the Dodgers won the 2026 World Series and completed the three-peat.
Now that the Dodgers' season has ended without a World Series title, the 37-year-old is ready to officially call it a career. Rojas began his career back in 2014 with the Dodgers. He was then traded to the Miami Marlins, and spent eight years there before returning to Los Angeles via trade ahead of the 2023 season.
Over the next four years, Rojas emerged as a key veteran leader in the Dodgers clubhouse, while also playing some of the best baseball of his career. Rojas had an OPS above .700 in each of the last three years. He played a critical role in the 2024 season that ended in the team's first World Series, hitting .283 with an OPS of .748 across 103 games.
Then, after appearing in another 114 games in the regular season in 2025, he was vital in that year's postseason, hitting .278 with an OPS of .760 across eight games. Rojas has said he wants to remain in the Dodgers organization in some capacity as a coach. It remains to be seen if he does that as soon as 2027. Rojas has also said he wants to be a manager in his future.
It wouldn't be a surprise to see him in a manager's chair sooner rather than later. Rojas retires as a two-time World Series champion and a career .260 hitter with 61 home runs, 386 RBIs and an OPS of .677. He was also an elite defender, and continued that high-level of play into the end of his career with the Dodgers.
